title: Review: Respiration; Homeostasis; The human nervous system
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank, except where marked for AQA GCSE Biology (8461) (status of the source: authored-gated-unreviewed). Terms and clues: 4.4.2-c05 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.5.1-c04 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.5.2-c07 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.4.2-c01 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition. Questions: 4.4.2-q04, 4.4.2-q10, 4.4.2-q13, 4.5.1-q03, 4.5.2-q03, 4.4.2-q02, 4.4.2-q09, 4.4.2-q12, 4.5.1-q02, 4.5.2-q02, 4.4.2-q01, 4.5.1-q01. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Anaerobic respiration
items.clue: Respiration in cells that takes place without oxygen, to transfer energy.

items.label: effector
items.clue: A muscle or gland that brings about a response which restores the optimum level.

items.label: Reflex action
items.clue: An automatic and rapid response to a stimulus that does not involve the conscious part of the brain.

items.label: Cellular respiration
items.clue: An exothermic reaction which is continuously occurring in living cells, transferring energy from glucose.

questions.stem: Which word equation represents aerobic respiration?

options.text: glucose + oxygen → lactic acid + water
carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen
glucose + oxygen → ethanol + carbon dioxide
glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water

questions.explanation: This is the equation given in the specification for aerobic respiration: glucose and oxygen are used and carbon dioxide and water are produced.

questions.stem: A sprinter's muscles are not supplied with enough oxygen during a race. What happens in the muscles?

options.text: lactic acid builds up and an oxygen debt forms
carbon dioxide builds up and an oxygen debt forms
ethanol builds up and an oxygen debt is formed
lactic acid builds up and more energy is made

questions.explanation: If insufficient oxygen is supplied, anaerobic respiration takes place in muscles; the incomplete oxidation of glucose causes a build up of lactic acid and creates an oxygen debt.

questions.stem: A plant cell synthesises protein. Which molecules does its metabolism use?

options.text: glucose and fatty acids, to make amino acids
glucose and nitrate ions, to make amino acids
glycerol and nitrate ions, to make amino acids
starch and nitrate ions, to make amino acids

questions.explanation: Metabolism includes the use of glucose and nitrate ions to form amino acids which in turn are used to synthesise proteins.

questions.stem: A person becomes cold and begins to shiver. Which structure is acting as the effector in this control system?

options.text: the muscles that contract to make the body shiver
the receptors that detect the fall in temperature
the brain that processes information from receptors
the nerves that carry impulses through the body

questions.explanation: Effectors are muscles or glands which bring about responses which restore optimum levels; here muscles contract to produce shivering.

questions.stem: In a reflex arc, what is the function of the relay neurone?

options.text: It carries the impulse to the conscious brain.
It links the sensory neurone to the motor neurone.
It carries the electrical impulse across the synapse.
It carries the impulse from the skin without the CNS.

questions.explanation: In a reflex arc the sensory neurone passes the impulse across a synapse to a relay neurone in the CNS, which passes it on to the motor neurone that carries the impulse to the effector.

questions.stem: How does anaerobic respiration in muscle cells compare with aerobic respiration?

options.text: far more energy transferred, and lactic acid made
less energy transferred, and lactic acid made
less energy transferred, and ethanol made as well
less energy transferred, and carbon dioxide made

questions.explanation: Anaerobic respiration in muscles is represented by glucose → lactic acid, and because the oxidation of glucose is incomplete much less energy is transferred than in aerobic respiration.

questions.stem: How does the body react to the increased demand for energy during exercise?

options.text: the heart rate, breathing rate and breath volume rise
the breathing rate rises but the heart rate stays steady
the heart rate rises but the breath volume is steady
the breath volume rises but the heart rate is steady

questions.explanation: The heart rate, breathing rate and breath volume increase during exercise to supply the muscles with more oxygenated blood.

questions.stem: How is a lipid molecule formed in metabolism?

options.text: from three glycerols and one fatty acid
from a single glycerol and three amino acids
from three fatty acids and one glucose
from one glycerol and three fatty acids

questions.explanation: Metabolism includes the formation of lipid molecules from a molecule of glycerol and three molecules of fatty acids.

questions.stem: The pancreas releases a hormone that lowers a high blood glucose concentration. Which statement about this control system is correct?

options.text: A nervous response restores the optimum level
A chemical response prevents the level changing
A chemical response restores the optimum level
A receptor response restores the optimum level

questions.explanation: Automatic control systems may involve nervous responses or chemical responses; a hormone released by the pancreas is a chemical response, and the optimum blood glucose concentration is restored.

questions.stem: Effectors in the human body may be:

options.text: muscles contracting or glands secreting
receptors detecting light and sound levels
skeletal muscles moving bones at a joint
neurones carrying impulses into the brain

questions.explanation: The CNS coordinates the response of effectors, which may be muscles contracting or glands secreting hormones.

options.text: an endothermic reaction happening in all living cells
an exothermic reaction happening during hard exercise
an exothermic reaction happening in all living cells
an exothermic reaction happening when we breathe in

questions.explanation: Cellular respiration is an exothermic reaction which is continuously occurring in living cells, transferring the energy needed for living processes.

questions.stem: During exercise a person's body temperature rises above its optimum level. Why does the body respond to bring the temperature back down?

options.text: To make the person feel comfortable when hot
To keep optimum conditions for enzyme action
To stop the internal conditions from changing
To let the receptors bring about the cooling

questions.explanation: Homeostasis maintains optimal conditions for enzyme action and all cell functions, so a temperature above the optimum is corrected.
